title: DoorDash to offer 'buy now, pay later,' but experts warn of risks
summary: Local TV news report on DoorDash's Klarna partnership, with experts warning BNPL could encourage reckless spending on food.

assertions.quote: when you look at the fine print that pizza may cost more than you expect

verdicts.note: This is the consistent finding across journalistic and CFPB analyses of how the 'free' pay-in-four product is actually funded.
KC Fed: longer-term BNPL loans can charge up to nearly 30% APR, and auto-repayments can trigger overdraft/NSF fees even on a nominally interest-free pay-in-four plan.

NBER: BNPL's 0% rate to the shopper is funded by the merchant, who pays for it through a fee covered by the sales and margin gains BNPL produces (the 'Robin Hood' price-discrimination mechanism) -- the 0% is not costless to produce.

assertions.quote: there's so many folks that would not qualify today for credit card

verdicts.note: This is the standard underwriting approach providers themselves describe, and why the product is marketed to people without strong credit.
KC Fed: BNPL loans require only a soft credit check with no effect on the consumer's score and can be approved even with no credit history, unlike credit cards' hard credit check.

assertions.quote: you're going to get a pizza today and you're going to have to pay for the whole month
BNPL offers of good option for that... but for big purchases, not fast food or groceries

verdicts.note: Financial educators commonly give this advice, but it is a judgment about prudent use rather than a strictly provable fact.
